# PREFIX-808 — Exact multi-edge cut projection, lattice saturation, and signed observer fibers

**Date:** 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai)  
**Line:** Enterprise Math / Research 6 portable direct continuation of PREFIX-807  
**Frozen scientific pin:** \`f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d\` (unchanged)  
**Historical research attribution:** \`EM-DIRECT-4660FF\` / \`RA-63E1066C3056A93898BE8E18\` (do not infer a new native CLAIM from this note)  
**Status:** AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_REGRESSION / NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED

## 1. Mathematical question and definitions

PREFIX-807 proves an integer interval for **one** selected named source edge with all other frozen assignments held fixed. Determine the *joint* attainable values of an arbitrary finite set of selected source edges, preserving named-source incidence and future signed observers. Coordinatewise intervals alone need not describe their correlations.

Let \(G=(U\sqcup V,E)\) be a finite **named bipartite multigraph**; distinct parallel edges are distinct indices. Each edge has an integral capacity \(K_e\ge 0\), and vertices have nonnegative integral demands \(R_i,S_j\). A full table \(x\in\mathbb Z^E\) is legal iff \(0\le x_e\le K_e\) and
\(\sum_{e\ni i}x_e=R_i\) for each \(i\in U\), \(\sum_{e\ni j}x_e=S_j\) for each \(j\in V\).
Assume total row and column demand agree. Let \(F,T\subset E\) be disjoint sets of frozen and selected edges, with frozen integer assignments \(f\) and proposed selected integer counts \(t\). Set \(H=E\setminus(F\cup T)\).

After subtracting all values in \(F\cup T\), let \(r_i(t)\) and \(s_j(t)\) be the remaining vertex demands. For any \(A\subseteq U\), \(B\subseteq V\), put
\[
C_H(A,V\setminus B)=\sum_{\substack{e=(i,j)\in H\\i\in A,\ j\notin B}}K_e.
\]
The quantities retain named parallel-edge multiplicity in the sum.

## 2. Theorem 808.1 — Exact joint integer cut certificate

A selected vector \(t\in\mathbb Z^T\) has a legal integral completion preserving every frozen edge if and only if:

1. \(0\le f_e\le K_e\) on \(F\) and \(0\le t_e\le K_e\) on \(T\);
2. all \(r_i(t),s_j(t)\) are nonnegative, with equal row/column total; and
3. for **every** pair \(A\subseteq U,B\subseteq V\),
\[
\boxed{\ \sum_{i\in A}r_i(t)-\sum_{j\in B}s_j(t)
\ \le C_H(A,V\setminus B).\ }\tag{808-C}
\]

This is a *finite system of explicit linear inequalities* in the jointly selected edge counts. More explicitly, writing \(R_i^F,S_j^F\) for the post-frozen demands, (808-C) becomes
\[
\sum_{e=(i,j)\in T}\bigl(1_{i\in A}-1_{j\in B}\bigr)t_e
\ \ge\sum_{i\in A}R_i^F-\sum_{j\in B}S_j^F-C_H(A,V\setminus B).
\tag{808-L}
\]
Consequently the joint integer projection can be computed from cuts without separately solving a completion problem for each integer vector. A violated inequality, together with \(A,B\), is an exact infeasibility witness.

**Proof.** Remove \(F\cup T\) and build the directed capacitated network with source arcs \(s\to i\) of capacity \(r_i(t)\), named interior arcs \(i\to j\) for each \(e\in H\) of capacity \(K_e\), and sink arcs \(j\to q\) of capacity \(s_j(t)\). For a source-side cut consisting of \(s\), row set \(A\) and column set \(B\), its capacity is
\[
\sum_{i\notin A}r_i(t)+C_H(A,V\setminus B)+\sum_{j\in B}s_j(t).
\]
It is at least \(N=\sum_i r_i(t)=\sum_j s_j(t)\) exactly when (808-C) holds. Thus the max-flow/min-cut theorem gives a flow of value \(N\) if and only if every such inequality holds. As the network capacities are integers, an *integral* maximum flow exists. Its interior named arc flows supply the missing legal integer counts, and the saturated source and sink arcs enforce all remaining margins. Conversely, a legal completion generates such a flow and therefore satisfies every cut inequality. This also works for named parallel arcs. QED.

## 3. Corollary 808.2 — Saturated lattice projection

Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^E\) be the *real* bounded capacity-and-margin transport polytope with the frozen \(F\) assignments imposed, and let \(Q=\pi_T(P)\). Then
\[
\boxed{\ \pi_T(P\cap\mathbb Z^E)=Q\cap\mathbb Z^T.\ }\tag{808-S}
\]
Moreover \(Q\) is an **integral polytope**, and the integer solutions of (808-C), residual nonnegativity and coordinate capacity bounds give its entire attainable lattice set.

**Proof.** For each integer \(t\in Q\), a real residual completion exists. Its feasibility implies the network cut inequalities, which by Theorem 808.1 yield an integral completion. This proves (808-S). The original transport polytope \(P\) is integral, by the total unimodularity of bipartite incidence constraints together with integral bounds (or the integral network-flow formulation). The linear image of the convex hull of its integer vertices is the convex hull of their integer projections; hence \(Q\) is integral. QED.

The theorem says that the *actual joint projected polytope* has no missing lattice points. It does **not** identify that polytope with the product of the separately attainable edge intervals; joint cuts may remove corners and entire slices of that product.

## 4. Counterexample — Marginal intervals lose joint provenance

Take the 2×2 complete named grid, all four capacities equal to 1 and row/column demands \(R=S=(1,1)\). Select the two top-row edges \(t=(x_{00},x_{01})\). Each selected edge separately attains both 0 and 1, but the row constraint forces
\[
\mathcal T=\{(1,0),(0,1)\},
\]
while \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\) are impossible. Each feasible selected pair has exactly one integral bottom-row completion. For the two-source observer \((Q_1,Q_2)=(x_{00},x_{01})\), the exact generating function is \(H(z_1,z_2)=z_1+z_2\). Multiplying the independent marginal generating functions would incorrectly introduce the missing joint states.

This is a provenance-sensitive *source-counting auxiliary model*. Its two selected variables are not a native Enterprise Math spatial plane. No X6 Cell/Link/Port/time equivalence is presumed.

## 5. Corollary 808.3 — Exact signed multi-observer decomposition

Let \(w_e\in\mathbb Z^d\) be a declared family of signed additive observation weights, and write \(z^{w}=\prod_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell^{w_\ell}\). For any frozen \(F\) vector \(f\), denote by \(H_H(r,s;z)\) the full Laurent generating function of the residual graph \(H\), counting *every* named integral completion with multiplicity. Then
\[
\boxed{
H_G(R,S;z\mid f)
=z^{\sum_{e\in F}f_ew_e}
\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
z^{\sum_{e\in T}t_ew_e}
H_H(r(t),s(t);z)
}\tag{808-H}
\]
where \(\mathcal T\) is **exactly** the integer cut-feasible set of Theorem 808.1. This follows from the bijection between complete named tables and a selected vector plus its residual named completion. Thus cut certificates are compatible with PREFIX-802 Laurent-suffix memoization, PREFIX-804 separator convolution, PREFIX-805 sufficient signatures and PREFIX-806 Hall filtering.

For a fixed graph, the cut system contains at most \(2^{|U|+|V|}\) row/column subset inequalities; precomputing their coefficients yields a direct \(O(|T|2^{|U|+|V|})\) candidate test, in addition to the residual bounds, while a violated cut gives a localized certificate. This bound concerns one candidate check and says nothing about the number of candidate vectors.

## 6. Independent exact finite regression

Self-contained Python 3 standard-library script:
\`research_notes/portable_direct/PREFIX808_R6_MULTI_EDGE_CUT_PROJECTION_CHECK.py\`.

Structured stdout from a completed local run:
\`research_notes/portable_direct/PREFIX808_R6_MULTI_EDGE_CUT_PROJECTION_RESULTS.json\`.

The checker exhaustively enumerates *all* capacity vectors and achievable margin fibers of: 2×2 with capacities 0..2; 2×3 with capacities 0..1; and 3×3 with capacities 0..1. For 2×2 and 2×3, it tests every pair and triple of selected edges; for 3×3 it tests selected pairs (0,4) and (2,6). The 2×2 pair tests also cover a further individually frozen named edge and every value observed in the fiber. A separate 2×2 graph with one *parallel* named source edge tests 880 selected pair vectors. All signed **two-observer histograms** use the explicit deterministic integer weights embedded in the checker, and for each cut-feasible selected vector the code independently enumerates every residual completion.

| Metric | Exact count |
|---|---:|
| Capacity patterns | 657 |
| Achievable margin fibers | 19,759 |
| Complete named source tables enumerated | 21,708 |
| Selected/frozen subfiber comparisons | 88,022 |
| Joint selected-vector candidates | 373,960 |
| Feasible joint vectors | 92,376 |
| Infeasible vectors excluded by cuts | 281,584 |
| Exact signed histogram comparisons | 92,376 |
| Additional parallel-edge vector checks | 880 |

All assertions passed with status \`ALL_EXACT_ASSERTIONS_PASSED\`. The 3×3 family covers exactly the two named selected-pair patterns stated above; the theoretical result allows arbitrary named graphs and selected sets. The experiment establishes finite code correctness on declared inputs and is independent of the universal max-flow proof.

## 7. Frontier, authority and next problem

This directly extends PREFIX-807 from one-source edge intervals to a joint source projection with exact cut descriptions and lattice saturation. The native X6 mapping remains an independent research question; P000, ACTIVE worldview, source joint-relation preservation, frozen science pin and historical task/CLAIM/Review authority are unchanged.

**Next discriminating unit:** Implement a cut-coefficient cache for selected separator edges and compare it against (i) repeated per-vector Hall/max-flow checks, (ii) the PREFIX-807 one-edge interval method, and (iii) PREFIX-805/806 signature-Hall grouping. On reproducible sparse/dense graphs, report full preprocessing + cut evaluation + residual histogram time, peak memory, source-multiplicity integrity, and where precomputing cuts ceases to pay off. Separately investigate scope-typed native X6 Cell/Link/Port/event-time embeddings only after preserving the required signed source identities and future operations.

**References:** PREFIX-807 (current prior source, originally published in \`research_notes/portable_direct/2026-11-15_r6_prefix807_exact_residual_edge_interval_certificates.md\`); current P000, \`definitions/ENTERPRISE_JOINT_RELATION_OBSERVER_PRESERVATION_20260905.json\`, ACTIVE account worldview, and \`docs/RESEARCH_CONTINUATION_PROTOCOL.md#current-normative-context\`. The math proof uses the integral maximum-flow/minimum-cut theorem and total unimodularity of bipartite incidence constraints; no external citation is needed for the standalone derivation presented here.
